must_remember: Proper length ($L_0$) is measured in the rest frame of the object, while relativistic length ($L$) is measured by a moving observer.
Length contraction occurs exclusively along the direction of relative motion, governed by the formula $L = L_0 \sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$.
Transverse dimensions perpendicular to the velocity vector remain invariant ($y = y_0$, $z = z_0$).
Length contraction is a reciprocal phenomenon; each inertial observer perceives the other's measuring rods as contracted.
Measuring moving length requires simultaneous determination of the positions of both ends in the observer's frame.

glossary.meaning: The length of an object measured in the frame of reference in which the object is at rest.
The length of an object measured by an observer moving at a constant relative velocity $v$ with respect to the object.
The factor $\gamma = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ by which lengths contract and time dilates in special relativity.
The dimension of an object perpendicular to the line of motion, which remains unaffected by length contraction.
The relation between two events happening at the same time; its relativity is the physical origin of length contraction.
